# ghedata

<!-- badges: start -->

[![License: CC BY
4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-CC_BY_4.0-lightgrey.svg)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of ghedata is to share data resources that document the work of the Global Health Engineering group at ETH Zurich. The data can be used for research, teaching, and learning purposes. The data is available as an R data package, in CSV and XLSX formats.

## Installation

You can install the development version of ghedata from
[GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("global-health-engineering/ghedata")
```

```{r}
## Run the following code in console if you don't have the packages
## install.packages(c("dplyr", "knitr", "readr", "stringr", "gt", "kableExtra"))
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(gt)
library(kableExtra)
library(ggthemes)
library(ggplot2)
```

Alternatively, you can download the individual datasets as a CSV or XLSX
file from the table below.

1.  Click Download CSV. A window opens that displays the CSV in
    your browser.
2.  Right-click anywhere inside the window and select "Save Page As...".
3.  Save the file in a folder of your choice.

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

extdata_path <- "https://github.com/global-health-engineering/ghedata/raw/main/inst/extdata/"

read_csv("data-raw/dictionary.csv") |> 
  distinct(file_name) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(file_name = str_remove(file_name, ".rda")) |> 
  dplyr::rename(dataset = file_name) |> 
  mutate(
    CSV = paste0("[Download CSV](", extdata_path, dataset, ".csv)"),
    XLSX = paste0("[Download XLSX](", extdata_path, dataset, ".xlsx)")
  ) |> 
  knitr::kable()

```

## Data

The package provides access to 11 tables, described below by topic.

```{r}
library(ghedata)
```

### people

The dataset `people` contains data about people that have worked for the group. This includes staff, as well as undergraduate student projects.

It has `r nrow(people)` observations and `r ncol(people)` variables.

```{r}
people |> 
  head(3) |> 
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::as_raw_html()
```

For an overview of the variable names, see the following table.

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
readr::read_csv("data-raw/dictionary.csv") |>
  dplyr::filter(file_name == "people.rda") |>
  dplyr::select(variable_name:description) |> 
  knitr::kable() |> 
  kableExtra::kable_styling("striped") |> 
  kableExtra::scroll_box(height = "200px")
```

### GitHub tables

Seven tables describe the work of the group on GitHub. They hold counts only and no name, login or email address of the person who made a commit.

- `github_organisations` has `r nrow(github_organisations)` rows, one per organisation, with the number of public and private repositories.
- `github_repositories` has `r nrow(github_repositories)` rows, one per public repository.
- `github_repository_types` has `r nrow(github_repository_types)` rows with the number of repositories per organisation, visibility, type and year of creation. It counts all `r format(sum(github_repository_types$repos), big.mark = ",")` repositories, private ones and student work included, and names none.
- `github_commits` has `r nrow(github_commits)` rows, one per organisation, visibility and month, with the number of commits on the default branches. Commits by people, by bots, automated pushes and merge commits each have their own column. Private repositories are counted and never named.
- `github_commits_by_type` has `r nrow(github_commits_by_type)` rows with the same commits per organisation, visibility, repository type and month.
- `github_commits_by_person` has `r nrow(github_commits_by_person)` rows, one per group member, with the number of commits over the last twelve full months. A person is a rank, never a name. In a small group a rank can still point to a person for someone who knows the group.
- `github_commits_by_members` has `r nrow(github_commits_by_members)` rows, one per month, with the number of commits by all group members together.

The data was read from GitHub on `r unique(github_organisations$snapshot_date)`.

The number of repositories by type, without the `r format(sum(github_repository_types$repos[github_repository_types$repository_type == "learner repository"]), big.mark = ",")` repositories of learners in courses and workshops:

```{r github-types}
github_repository_types |>
  dplyr::filter(repository_type != "learner repository") |>
  dplyr::count(repository_type, visibility, wt = repos) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = visibility, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(total = public + private) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(total)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The commits made by people, by repository type and year. The year `r format(max(github_commits_by_type$month), "%Y")` runs up to `r format(max(github_commits_by_type$month), "%B")`.

```{r github-commits-by-type}
github_commits_by_type |>
  dplyr::mutate(year = format(month, "%Y")) |>
  dplyr::count(repository_type, year, wt = commits) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = n, values_fill = 0, names_sort = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(total = rowSums(dplyr::across(-repository_type))) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(total)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

Commits by bots and automated pushes are counted apart. An automated push is a commit that a device or a script makes under the account of a person, for example a sensor that uploads its readings every hour.

```{r github-commit-classes}
github_commits |>
  dplyr::mutate(year = format(month, "%Y")) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    people = sum(commits),
    bots = sum(commits_bot),
    automated = sum(commits_automated),
    merge = sum(commits_merge),
    .by = year
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

`github_commit_change()` compares the commits of the last 12 complete months with the 12 months before.

```{r github-change}
github_commit_change() |> 
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

For an overview of the variable names, see the following table.

```{r github-dictionary, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
readr::read_csv("data-raw/dictionary.csv") |>
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_starts(file_name, "github_")) |>
  dplyr::select(file_name:description) |>
  knitr::kable() |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling("striped") |>
  kableExtra::scroll_box(height = "200px")
```

### Proposals table

One table holds the funding proposals of the group. It holds no name of a person.

- `proposals` has `r nrow(proposals)` rows, one per proposal since `r format(min(proposals$submitted_date, na.rm = TRUE), "%Y")`, with the status, the funder, the dates of submission and answer, and the budget in its currency and in Swiss francs. `r sum(proposals$status == "accepted", na.rm = TRUE)` proposals were accepted. The requested budgets add up to CHF `r format(round(sum(proposals$budget_chf, na.rm = TRUE)), big.mark = ",")`, of which CHF `r format(round(sum(proposals$budget_chf[proposals$status == "accepted"], na.rm = TRUE)), big.mark = ",")` were accepted. `r sum(is.na(proposals$budget_chf))` proposals have no budget on record, so the sums are lower bounds.

### Reach table

One table holds what was published on Zenodo and how often it was viewed and downloaded. It holds no name of an author.

- `zenodo_records` has `r nrow(zenodo_records)` rows, one per record on Zenodo by a creator from the group or in the openwashdata community, with `r format(sum(zenodo_records$views), big.mark = ",")` views and `r format(sum(zenodo_records$downloads), big.mark = ",")` downloads in total. The counts were read on `r unique(zenodo_records$snapshot_date)`.

## Example

```{r}
library(ghedata)

undergrad_students <- people |> 
  filter(b_m_student == "yes") |>
  filter(!is.na(thesis_title)) 
```

So far, GHE has supervised `r nrow(undergrad_students)` projects of which `r nrow(undergrad_students[undergrad_students$degree == "bsc",])` were done by BSc and `r nrow(undergrad_students[undergrad_students$degree == "msc",])` by MSc students.

```{r}
undergrad_students |> 
  count(degree, year) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = n, label = n, fill = degree, color = degree)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  geom_text(position=position_dodge(width=0.9), 
            vjust=-0.5,
            show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "",
       y = "Number of students") +
  scale_fill_colorblind() +
  scale_color_colorblind() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_blank())
```
